# The least number of exterior conjugates in groups generated by small units and at the square endpoint

<a id="statement"></a>
## Exterior roots counted strictly

Write \(l(x)\) for the number of distinct conjugates of \(x\) of modulus strictly greater than one, \(m=\log M\) for total logarithmic Mahler measure, and \(D(\mathcal F)\) for the group of torsion twists and radicals of finite monomials in conjugates from a family \(\mathcal F\).
Take a nonempty family of nontorsion units of uniformly sufficiently small positive \(m\).
For each member use its [chain of compressed reciprocal block products](Yin_C_G0901_v93.md#descent) and let \(b_0\) be the smallest block size at any term of any chain.
Let \(L\) be the minimum of \(l(x)\) over all nontorsion \(x\in D(\mathcal F)\).
If \(L<(b_0-1)/4\), then
\[
       L=\min_{w\in\mathcal F} l(z_s(w)),
\]
where \(z_s(w)\) is the terminal term of the chain for \(w\).
Some terminal unit attaining \(L\) has a neutral conjugate, degree at most that of its own input and positive total log measure at most that input's.
This applies to every fixed bound on \(L\) as the uniform measure ceiling tends to zero, since \(b_0\to\infty\).
In particular it applies to the combined conjugate groups of all noncyclotomic factors of an integer polynomial of sufficiently small positive total measure, after removing possible zero roots.

There is a different exact minimum for a compressed reciprocal Perron unit \(r\) with the [oriented square pattern](Yin_C_G0901_v109.md#minimal).
Write \(d=2ub\) for its degree, with \(u\) canonical blocks of \(b\) inverse pairs, and suppose its half products are torsion and only one block is nonneutral as in that pattern.
At bounded total measure and sufficiently large \(d\) in terms of the bound, **every** nontorsion \(x\in D(r)\) has at least \(b\) exterior conjugates.
On the rational lines of single conjugates the count is a positive integer multiple of \(b\), with \(b\) attained by \(r\).
On every other line,
\[
                         l(x)\ge b(b-2)/8 .
\]
In fact all joint distributions of log moduli in \(D(r)\) are symmetric under simultaneous negation, with the distribution taken over the embeddings of a common normal field for any finite tuple.
These conclusions allow witnesses of unrestricted measure, degree and reciprocity.
They give no uniform lower bound for \(m(r)\).

<a id="descent"></a>
## Attaining a small minimum on a terminal term

Choose \(x\) attaining \(L\) and restrict to a finite subfamily supporting it.
Apply the [successive normal orbit products](Yin_C_G0901_v119.md#counts) to its active constituent spaces, including compression by products of torsion classes.
The number of strictly exterior conjugates cannot increase at either operation.
Within a torsion class the moduli agree, and a product of modulus greater than one over a normal subgroup orbit requires a strictly exterior factor in that orbit.
The orbits in this partition are disjoint, and repetitions among their products only decrease the count.
The resulting nontorsion \(y\) has its class in one actual leading constituent \(W\) attached to a term \(z_j\) of one of the original chains, and \(l(y)\le L\).

Write \(b\) for the block size of this term.
For a noncoordinate class in the independent signed or oriented sum-zero model of \(W\), the [orbit and height inequalities](Yin_C_G0901_v115.md#pure) give \(l(y)\ge(b-1)/4\); the argument there counts strictly positive logs as well as strictly negative logs in this case.
Thus \([y]\) is a nonzero rational multiple of a coordinate in \(W\), using the projected coordinate when the block is oriented.
Its orbit consists of all \(2ub\) signed coordinates, equally represented among the embeddings. [Signed coordinate orbit](Yin_C_G0901_v113.md#rank)
Its log moduli therefore occur in opposite pairs.
Their rational rank is at most \(l(y)\), since the positive logs span, and equals \(\dim W^c\) for ordinary complex conjugation \(c\) by the [radial rank formula](Yin_C_G0901_v62.md#modules).

The independent signed case is already terminal.
In the oriented case an exchanged pair of blocks contributes \(b-1\) fixed dimensions on \(W\), and a fixed block with positive orientation sign contributes at least \(b/2-1\).
Both exceed \(L\).
Hence every block is fixed with negative sign, and \(c\) negates the entire space generated by half products.
Every conjugate half product then has modulus one, so is torsion by Kronecker. [Fixed dimensions and the block products](Yin_C_G0901_v89.md#oriented)
This term too is terminal.
In both cases the actual compressed \(z_j\) has those same signed classes as its conjugate orbit.
Scaling them by a nonzero rational changes neither the number of exterior entries nor the symmetry between positive and negative logs, before accounting for the equal embedding multiplicities of \(y\).
It follows that \(l(y)\) is a positive integer multiple of \(l(z_j)\).
The inequalities \(L\le l(z_j)\le l(y)\le L\) give equality, and \(2l(z_j)<2ub=\deg z_j\) gives a neutral conjugate by reciprocity.
The bounds on degree and measure are those of its own chain.

<a id="symmetry"></a>
## Reversing all log moduli at once in the square pattern

Orient the active block by its half containing \(r\).
That half has one exterior root and \(b-1\) interior roots; its inverse half supplies the other \(b-1\) exterior roots, so \(l(r)=b\).
The actual conjugate class space \(V\) is the direct sum of the coordinate-sum-zero representations on the \(u\) blocks, with independent supported \(A_b\) actions.
Indeed the half products are torsion, compression separates the distinct coordinates, and the [irreducibility argument](Yin_C_G0901_v84.md#modules) gives precisely this representation under these hypotheses.
The log-modulus functional vanishes on every other block, since all its roots are neutral.

There is a pair of equal log moduli among the \(b\) roots in the active half for sufficiently large \(d\).
Indeed \(u\ll(\log(3d))^{212}\) with constant depending on the measure ceiling, by the [canonical block bound](Yin_C_G0345_v270.md#statement).
The total number of real roots is \(O(\sqrt{d\log(3d)})=o(b)\) by the [real-place estimate](Yin_C_G0901_v65.md#statement).
Complex conjugation preserves this half because it fixes \(r\), so it pairs a nonreal member with its distinct conjugate in the same half.
The permutation exchanging those two labels fixes the entire list of log moduli.

Choose a Galois automorphism carrying \(r\) to \(r^{-1}\).
It preserves the active block with negative orientation sign and some permutation of its \(b\) labels.
Postcompose with a supported even permutation so that its resulting permutation is the identity if the original permutation is even, and the transposition just exhibited if it is odd.
Call the composite \(h\).
It negates the log-modulus functional on the active block and preserves the complementary sum on which that functional vanishes.
Thus \(\log|h v|=-\log|v|\) for all multiplicative classes \(v\in V\), with logs interpreted by rational homogeneity.
Given finitely many actual elements of \(D(r)\), extend \(h\) to a common finite normal field containing them and the original roots.
Left multiplication by this lift takes the tuple of logs at any embedding to its negative, proving the joint symmetry with multiplicities.

<a id="count"></a>
## Counting exterior roots on every other line

For a nontorsion \(x\in D(r)\) its conjugate span equals \(V\) by irreducibility, and \(t=\dim V=u(b-1)\).
Put \(R=\dim V^c\).
On the active half \(c\) acts by an involutive permutation with positive sign; on its sum-zero space this gives at least \(b/2-1\) fixed dimensions.
The [projection count over embeddings](Yin_C_G0901_v64.md#degree) gives
\[
                  (\deg x)R\le 2l(x)t .
\]
Indeed its proof uses the number of nonneutral embeddings, which is exactly \(2l(x)\) here by the preceding symmetry, also for a nonreciprocal \(x\).
Off the coordinate lines, \(\deg x\ge ub(b-1)/2\) by the [orbit count](Yin_C_G0901_v84.md#orbit).
Substitution gives \(l(x)\ge b(b-2)/8>b\) for \(b>10\).
On a coordinate line each class in the orbit of a rationally scaled original root has the same number of actual embeddings above it.
Reciprocity of \(r\) therefore gives \(l(x)=b\,\deg(x)/d\), with \(\deg(x)/d\) a positive integer.
